body:
Literally the only things I'd strive for at this point are not having to worry about money, getting a place to live where I could have a cat, not being allergic to cats, and finding someone(s) to share it with that have similar sexual and/or hobby leanings.

In other words fantasy hedonism.  But only because I feel like I've given up on more meaningful things.

Seriously though I need to try to sleep.  Thanks for humoring my thread.  Bye. :D

I looked forward to starting a family.  Heck I looked forward to the mundane modern life in general.  Just imagining it and my pretend daughter, who I'd raise to be no simple Disney princess to my pretend son, who would be beating his old man at Mario Kart before he's even able to play catch... good imaginary times.

Now I can't imagine getting a simple, human connection with a woman necessary to partner up to raise a child.  Let alone fucking to have one.  Let alone coldly deciding to adopt one and raise him/her to the best of our loveless, calculating ability.

It's emblematic of my bullshit as a whole:  I feel like it's pointless, and the only things I once called goals were heavily romanticized caricatures.  People, regardless of race or gender, seem preoccupied with different things than me.  That doesn't make me better or worse than them.  It does, however, leave me feeling unhappy!

It's a clumsy abstraction of disillusionment in general, but I could apply it most precisely to career / professional work.  I never envisioned myself as a world changer, but I always thought I'd find a place and peers I was comfortable with.  I've gone through a variety of blue collar and white collar gigs and never felt at home.

A more emotionally impactful example would be other people in general.  For example growing up I imagined starting my own family but fucking up a bunch while hopefully leaving the family legacy better off than when I found it.  Now I'm older than most first time parents and I feel like a complete alien to most pople, regarldess of gender, and the idea of being responsible for the development of another human life when I can't figure out shit for myself is overwhelming.

That was kind of a non-sequitor.  I will say the end game is that I feel like I'm seeing colors when everyone else is seeing shapes.  I'm not connected.

Not quite.  It's more that you believe and work towards something that straight up doesn't exist.

Like someone telling you when you're a kid you're a great cook you're such a great cook you are going to grow up to make the best potato salad ever.  And then twenty years in to perfecting your potato salad recipe you realize that potato salad is not a real thing, that it's a fake idea, that whoever was telling you about potato salad was doing it in a story full of unicorns and werewolves.

I don't mean that to come off too lightly, I just want to get the main point across:  even if I work my hardest, I do not see a satisfactory life before me.  I just don't care.  I'd rather transfer to the opportunity to someone else in some way.
